- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates price; add 3–8% bias upward to reflect supply constraint.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and model is still rising, force downward correction by 5–10% to align with sentiment drift.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often overestimates price; apply 5–15% downward bias to reflect event saturation or supply pressure.  
- If model forecast is flat or trending slowly but true price shows strong upward movement, assume sentiment is lagging; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% to capture sentiment lag effect.
